newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB SELLS IRAN 800,000 T WHEAT AT US$135 FOB-TRADE.
newsitem.headline: CWB SELLS IRAN 800,000 T WHEAT AT US$135 FOB-TRADE.

text.p: Iran bought 800,000 tonnes of milling wheat from the Canadian Wheat Board at US$135 FOB St. Lawrence for shipment between September and December, trade sources said.
"There was a large trade of wheat to Iran two or three weeks ago, about 800,000 tonnes for September, October, November and December positions," one source said.
Two sources said the sale took place near the end of July when the wheat market was near its lows and was done at US$135 a tonne FOB St. Lawrence.

"The Wheat Board deals with Iran direct but I heard word of this a couple of weeks ago. It's probably No3 CWRS (Canada Western Red Spring wheat), it's the most abundant of classes in old crop carry out," a second source said.

Iran was the CWB's largest wheat purchaser in 1996/97 (Aug/July) buying 2.027 million tonnes of milling wheat and was expected to buy about the same amount in 1998/97, CWB chief commissioner Lorne Hehn said last week.
"We can neither confirm nor deny talk of that sale," CWB spokeswoman Tracey Bryksa said.
The CWB was not likely able to access enough supplies of feed barley to take part in Tuesday's optional-origin tender for 50,000 tonnes to Iran, one source said.
"The Board withdrew all of their wheat offers yesterday and they're back today with different positions than they had and that suggests they've done some business with someone," a third source said.
